1	"""Persistent, thread-safe job-to-offer match ledger."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import contextlib
6	import json
7	import os
8	import tempfile
9	import threading
10	from typing import Any, Callable
11	
12	from . import jobs as _jobs
13	from . import offers as _offers
14	from ._jsonio import strict_loads
15	
16	__all__ = ["match"]
17	
18	_VERSION = 1
19	_MATCH_FIELDS = ("job_id", "resource_id")
20	_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "matches", "idempotency")
21	
22	
23	class _Store:
24	    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
25	        self.realpath = realpath
26	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
27	
28	
29	_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
30	_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}
31	
32	
33	def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
34	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
35	    with _stores_lock:
36	        store = _stores.get(realpath)
37	        if store is None:
38	            store = _Store(realpath)
39	            _stores[realpath] = store
40	        return store
41	
42	
43	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
44	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
45	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
46	
47	
48	def _load_registry(
49	    realpath: str,
50	    validate: Callable[[object], tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], Any]],
51	    kind: str,
52	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], Any]:
53	    # Unlike the registries themselves, match() requires the jobs and offers
54	    # files to exist, so FileNotFoundError (and any other OSError) propagates.
55	    with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
56	        text = handle.read()
57	    try:
58	        data = strict_loads(text)
59	    except ValueError as exc:
60	        raise ValueError(
61	            f"{kind} file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
62	    return validate(data)
63	
64	
65	def _validate_ledger(
66	    data: object,
67	    job_ids: dict[str, Any],
68	    resource_ids: dict[str, Any],
69	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, str]], dict[str, str]]:
70	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
71	        raise ValueError("ledger root must be an object with keys "
72	                         "version, matches and idempotency")
73	
74	    version = data["version"]
75	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
76	        raise ValueError("unsupported ledger version")
77	
78	    matches_raw = data["matches"]
79	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
80	    if not isinstance(matches_raw, dict) or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict):
81	        raise ValueError("matches and idempotency must be objects")
82	
83	    matches: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
84	    for name, record in matches_raw.items():
85	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
86	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
87	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record.keys()) != set(_MATCH_FIELDS):
88	            raise ValueError("match record has invalid fields")
89	        if record["job_id"] != name:
90	            raise ValueError("match record id does not match its key")
91	        resource_id = record["resource_id"]
92	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
93	            raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
94	        if name not in job_ids:
95	            raise ValueError("match record must reference a registered job")
96	        if resource_id not in resource_ids:
97	            raise ValueError("match record must reference a registered offer")
98	        matches[name] = {"job_id": name, "resource_id": resource_id}
99	
100	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
101	    referenced: set[str] = set()
102	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
103	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
104	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
105	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in matches:
106	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a recorded match")
107	        if job_id in referenced:
108	            raise ValueError("job matched under more than one idempotency key")
109	        referenced.add(job_id)
110	        idempotency[key] = job_id
111	
112	    return matches, idempotency
113	
114	
115	def _load_ledger(
116	    realpath: str,
117	    job_ids: dict[str, Any],
118	    resource_ids: dict[str, Any],
119	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, str]], dict[str, str]]:
120	    try:
121	        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
122	            text = handle.read()
123	    except FileNotFoundError:
124	        return {}, {}
125	
126	    try:
127	        data = strict_loads(text)
128	    except ValueError as exc:
129	        raise ValueError(f"ledger file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
130	    return _validate_ledger(data, job_ids, resource_ids)
131	
132	
133	def _atomic_write(
134	    realpath: str,
135	    matches: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
136	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
137	) -> None:
138	    payload = {
139	        "version": _VERSION,
140	        "matches": {name: matches[name] for name in sorted(matches)},
141	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
142	    }
143	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
144	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
145	
146	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
147	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".ledger-",
148	                                    suffix=".tmp")
149	    try:
150	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
151	            handle.write(text)
152	            handle.flush()
153	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
154	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
155	    except BaseException:
156	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
157	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
158	        raise
159	
160	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
161	    try:
162	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
163	    finally:
164	        os.close(dir_fd)
165	
166	
167	def match(
168	    jobs: str,
169	    offers: str,
170	    ledger: str,
171	    job_id: str,
172	    key: str,
173	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
174	    """Match a registered job to the greenest feasible offer idempotently.
175	
176	    Candidates are offers whose region is permitted by the job's
177	    residency_regions and whose remaining capacity (capacity_wh minus the
178	    energy already allocated in the ledger) covers the job's energy_wh;
179	    the winner is the first by ascending carbon_intensity, unit_cost and
180	    resource_id. Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries
181	    job_id and resource_id; ``created`` is ``True`` for a new match and
182	    ``False`` when the idempotency key replays a match for the same job
183	    (which allocates no further capacity).
184	    """
185	    for value in (jobs, offers, ledger, job_id, key):
186	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
187	            raise ValueError("jobs, offers, ledger, job_id and key must be "
188	                             "non-empty strings")
189	
190	    store = _get_store(ledger)
191	    with store.lock:
192	        job_records, _ = _load_registry(
193	            os.path.realpath(jobs), _jobs._validate_structure, "jobs registry")
194	        if job_id not in job_records:
195	            raise KeyError(job_id)
196	        job = job_records[job_id]
197	
198	        offer_records, _ = _load_registry(
199	            os.path.realpath(offers), _offers._validate_structure,
200	            "offers registry")
201	        matches, idempotency = _load_ledger(
202	            store.realpath, job_records, offer_records)
203	
204	        existing = idempotency.get(key)
205	        if existing is not None:
206	            if existing != job_id:
207	                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
208	                                 "different job")
209	            return dict(matches[job_id]), False
210	        if job_id in matches:
211	            raise ValueError("job is already matched under another "
212	                             "idempotency key")
213	
214	        allocated: dict[str, int] = {}
215	        for record in matches.values():
216	            resource_id = record["resource_id"]
217	            allocated[resource_id] = (
218	                allocated.get(resource_id, 0)
219	                + job_records[record["job_id"]]["energy_wh"])
220	
221	        allowed = set(job["residency_regions"])
222	        needed = job["energy_wh"]
223	        best: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
224	        for resource_id, offer in offer_records.items():
225	            if offer["region"] not in allowed:
226	                continue
227	            if offer["capacity_wh"] - allocated.get(resource_id, 0) < needed:
228	                continue
229	            candidate = (offer["carbon_intensity"], offer["unit_cost"],
230	                         resource_id)
231	            if best is None or candidate < best:
232	                best = candidate
233	        if best is None:
234	            raise LookupError("no feasible offer for job")
235	
236	        record = {"job_id": job_id, "resource_id": best[2]}
237	        matches[job_id] = record
238	        idempotency[key] = job_id
239	        _atomic_write(store.realpath, matches, idempotency)
240	        return dict(record), True

1	"""Strict JSON decoding shared by the persistent registries.
2	
3	The only difference from :func:`json.loads` is that number tokens whose
4	lexical form is a negative zero (``-0``, ``-0.0``, ``-0e2`` ...) are rejected.
5	``json.loads`` silently normalizes ``-0`` to the integer ``0`` and ``-0.0``
6	to a non-negative float, which would let two byte-different files compare
7	equal; the registries instead treat such literals as malformed input. The
8	hooks only see number tokens, so a ``-0`` appearing inside a string is never
9	inspected.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import json
15	
16	__all__ = ["strict_loads", "finite_loads"]
17	
18	
19	def _is_negative_zero(token: str) -> bool:
20	    body = token.lstrip()
21	    if not body.startswith("-"):
22	        return False
23	    # A signed numeric token is negative zero exactly when its value is zero;
24	    # -0.5 stays non-zero, while every spelling of -0 (fraction/exponent) maps
25	    # to zero.
26	    return float(body) == 0.0
27	
28	
29	def _parse_int(token: str) -> int:
30	    if _is_negative_zero(token):
31	        raise ValueError("negative-zero number literal is not allowed")
32	    return int(token)
33	
34	
35	def _parse_float(token: str) -> float:
36	    if _is_negative_zero(token):
37	        raise ValueError("negative-zero number literal is not allowed")
38	    return float(token)
39	
40	
41	def strict_loads(text: str) -> object:
42	    """Parse JSON, raising ValueError on negative-zero number literals."""
43	    return json.loads(text, parse_int=_parse_int, parse_float=_parse_float)
44	
45	
46	def _reject_constant(token: str) -> float:
47	    # Only NaN/Infinity/-Infinity reach the constant hook; they are not
48	    # finite numbers and never valid in a verified document.
49	    raise ValueError("non-finite number literal is not allowed")
50	
51	
52	def finite_loads(text: str) -> object:

1	"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process resource-supply registry.
2	
3	One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
4	market:
5	
6	* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
7	  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
8	* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
9	* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
10	  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.
11	
12	:func:`publish` appends a new version under an idempotency key,
13	:func:`get` reads one resource record back by id and optional version,
14	and :func:`feasible` joins a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file with the
15	supply file under both shared locks to rank the resources that can
16	serve one accepted job at an evaluation moment. The supply file is
17	never rewritten by the read paths, and a version-1 ``jobs.register``
18	file is not a supply file.
19	"""

66	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
67	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
68	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

71	@contextlib.contextmanager
72	def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
73	    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
74	    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
75	    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
76	    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
77	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
78	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
79	    try:
80	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
81	        try:
82	            yield
83	        finally:
84	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
85	    finally:
86	        os.close(fd)

89	def _check_values(resource: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
90	    region = resource["region"]
91	    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
92	        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
93	
94	    capacity = resource["capacity"]
95	    if not _is_plain_int(capacity) or capacity <= 0:
96	        raise ValueError("capacity must be a non-boolean positive integer")
97	
98	    for name in ("start", "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
99	        value = resource[name]
100	        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
101	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
102	                             "integer")
103	    if resource["start"] > resource["end"]:
104	        raise ValueError("start must not be later than end")
105	
106	    residency = resource["residency"]
107	    if not isinstance(residency, list) or not residency:
108	        raise ValueError("residency must be a non-empty list")
109	    seen: set[str] = set()
110	    for entry in residency:
111	        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry:
112	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
113	        if entry in seen:
114	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
115	        seen.add(entry)
116	    # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
117	    if residency != sorted(residency):
118	        raise ValueError("residency regions must be sorted by code point")
119	    if region not in seen:
120	        raise ValueError("residency regions must contain the resource region")

123	def _normalize_resource(resource: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
124	    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
125	            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_RESOURCE_FIELDS):
126	        raise ValueError("resource must be an object with exactly "
127	                         "resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, "
128	                         "unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency")
129	
130	    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
131	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
132	        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
133	
134	    normalized: dict[str, Any] = {
135	        "resource_id": resource_id,
136	        "region": resource["region"],
137	        "capacity": resource["capacity"],
138	        "start": resource["start"],
139	        "end": resource["end"],
140	        "unit_cost": resource["unit_cost"],
141	        "carbon_intensity": resource["carbon_intensity"],
142	        "residency": resource["residency"],
143	    }
144	    _check_values(normalized)
145	    normalized["residency"] = list(normalized["residency"])

155	def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
156	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
157	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
158	]:
159	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
160	        raise ValueError("supply file root must be an object with keys "
161	                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")
162	
163	    version = data["version"]
164	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
165	        raise ValueError("unsupported supply file version")
166	
167	    history_raw = data["history"]
168	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
169	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
170	    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
171	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
172	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
173	        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
174	    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
175	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
176	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
177	
178	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
179	    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
180	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
181	            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
182	        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
183	            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
184	                             "per resource")
185	        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
186	        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
187	            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
188	                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
189	                raise ValueError("resource record has invalid fields")
190	            if record["resource_id"] != resource_id:
191	                raise ValueError("resource record id does not match its key")
192	            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
193	                    or record["version"] != index:
194	                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
195	            _check_values(record)
196	            if records and record["start"] <= records[-1]["start"]:
197	                raise ValueError("resource starts must increase across "
198	                                 "versions")
199	            records.append({
200	                "resource_id": resource_id,
201	                "version": index,
202	                "region": record["region"],
203	                "capacity": record["capacity"],
204	                "start": record["start"],
205	                "end": record["end"],
206	                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
207	                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
208	                "residency": list(record["residency"]),
209	            })
210	        history[resource_id] = records
211	
212	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
213	    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():
214	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
215	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
216	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
217	                or resource_id not in history:
218	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
219	                             "resource")
220	        idempotency[key] = resource_id
221	
222	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
223	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
224	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
225	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
226	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
227	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
228	            raise ValueError("publish audit event has invalid fields")
229	        event_key = event["key"]
230	        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
231	        event_version = event["version"]
232	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
233	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
234	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
235	                or resource_id not in history:
236	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
237	                             "resource")
238	        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
239	                or event_version > len(history[resource_id]):
240	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
241	                             "version")
242	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "resource_id": resource_id,
243	                       "version": event_version}
244	
245	    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
246	    # idempotency key binds one resource and one publish event, the map
247	    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version
248	    # is bound to exactly one event.
249	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
250	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
251	    for key, resource_id in idempotency.items():
252	        if events[key]["resource_id"] != resource_id:
253	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
254	                             "entry")
255	    published = {(resource_id, record["version"])
256	                 for resource_id, records in history.items()
257	                 for record in records}
258	    bound = {(event["resource_id"], event["version"])
259	             for event in events.values()}
260	    if bound != published:
261	        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
262	                         "audit event")
263	
264	    return history, idempotency, events
265

267	def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
268	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
269	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
270	]:
271	    try:
272	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
273	            raw = handle.read()
274	    except FileNotFoundError:
275	        return {}, {}, {}, None
276	
277	    try:
278	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
279	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
280	        raise ValueError(
281	            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
282	    try:
283	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
284	        data = finite_loads(text)
285	    except ValueError as exc:
286	        raise ValueError(
287	            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
288	    history, idempotency, events = _validate_structure(data)
289	    return history, idempotency, events, raw

292	def _serialize(
293	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
294	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
295	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
296	) -> bytes:
297	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
298	    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
299	    payload = {
300	        "version": _VERSION,
301	        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
302	                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
303	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
304	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
305	    }
306	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
307	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
308	    return text.encode("utf-8")

311	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
312	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
313	    try:
314	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
315	    finally:
316	        os.close(dir_fd)

319	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
320	                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
321	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
322	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
323	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
324	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
325	    try:
326	        if old_bytes is None:
327	            try:
328	                os.unlink(realpath)
329	            except FileNotFoundError:
330	                pass
331	        else:
332	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
333	                dir=directory, prefix=".resources-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
334	            try:
335	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
336	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
337	                    handle.flush()
338	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
339	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
340	            except BaseException:
341	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
342	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
343	                raise
344	        _fsync_directory(directory)
345	    except OSError as recovery:
346	        raise recovery from first
347	
348	
349	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
350	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
351	    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
352	    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
353	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
354	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
355	    # byte-for-byte.
356	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
357	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
358	        dir=directory, prefix=".resources-", suffix=".tmp")
359	    try:
360	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
361	            handle.write(payload)
362	            handle.flush()
363	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
364	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
365	    except BaseException:
366	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
367	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
368	        raise
369	    try:
370	        _fsync_directory(directory)
371	    except BaseException as first:
372	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
373	        raise

376	def publish(
377	    path: str,
378	    resource: dict[str, object],
379	    idempotency_key: str,
380	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
381	    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.
382	
383	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
384	    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
385	    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
386	    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
387	    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
388	    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
389	    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
390	    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
391	    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
392	
393	    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
394	    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
395	    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
396	    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
397	    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
398	    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
399	    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
400	    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
401	    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
402	    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
403	    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
404	
405	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
406	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
407	    version, structure, ordering or references) raises ``ValueError``;
408	    any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Calls serialize
409	    across threads and processes per resolved real path.
410	    """
411	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
412	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
413	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
414	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
415	    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
416	    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]
417	
418	    store = _get_store(path)
419	    with store.lock:
420	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
421	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
422	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
423	            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
424	                store.realpath)
425	
426	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
427	            if existing_id is not None:
428	                event = events[idempotency_key]
429	                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
430	                if {field: existing[field]
431	                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
432	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
433	                                     "a different resource")
434	                return dict(existing), False
435	
436	            versions = history.get(resource_id)
437	            if versions is None:
438	                versions = []
439	                history[resource_id] = versions
440	                version = 1
441	            else:
442	                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
443	                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
444	                                     "versions")
445	                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1
446	
447	            record: dict[str, Any] = {
448	                "resource_id": resource_id,
449	                "version": version,
450	                "region": normalized["region"],
451	                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
452	                "start": normalized["start"],
453	                "end": normalized["end"],
454	                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
455	                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
456	                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
457	            }
458	            versions.append(record)
459	            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
460	            events[idempotency_key] = {
461	                "key": idempotency_key,
462	                "resource_id": resource_id,
463	                "version": version,
464	            }
465	            _commit_file(store.realpath,
466	                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
467	            return dict(record), True
468

470	def get(
471	    path: str,
472	    resource_id: str,
473	    version: int | None = None,
474	) -> dict[str, object]:
475	    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.
476	
477	    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
478	    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
479	    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
480	    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
481	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file raises ``ValueError``; an
482	    unknown resource id raises ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown
483	    version ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure
484	    raises ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record
485	    is a fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start,
486	    end, unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
487	    """
488	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
489	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
490	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
491	        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
492	    if version is not None \
493	            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
494	        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")
495	
496	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
497	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
498	        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
499	    if raw is None:
500	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
501	    versions = history.get(resource_id)
502	    if versions is None:
503	        raise KeyError(resource_id)
504	    if version is None:
505	        return dict(versions[-1])
506	    if version > len(versions):
507	        raise KeyError(version)
508	    return dict(versions[version - 1])

511	def feasible(
512	    job_path: str,
513	    supply_path: str,
514	    job_id: str,
515	    at: int,
516	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
517	    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.
518	
519	    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
520	    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
521	    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
522	    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
523	    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
524	    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.
525	
526	    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
527	    an invalid file raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
528	    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
529	    ``OSError``.
530	
531	    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
532	    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
533	    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
534	    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
535	    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
536	    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
537	    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
538	    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
539	    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
540	    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
541	    candidate the list is empty.
542	    """
543	    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
544	        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
545	    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
546	        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
547	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
548	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
549	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
550	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
551	
552	    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
553	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
554	    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
555	    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
556	    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
557	        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
558	            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))
559	
560	        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
561	            job_real)
562	        if job_raw is None:
563	            raise FileNotFoundError(
564	                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")

"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process resource-supply registry.

One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
market:

* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.

:func:`publish` appends a new version under an idempotency key,
:func:`get` reads one resource record back by id and optional version,
and :func:`feasible` joins a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file with the
supply file under both shared locks to rank the resources that can
serve one accepted job at an evaluation moment. The supply file is
never rewritten by the read paths, and a version-1 ``jobs.register``
file is not a supply file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import fcntl
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Iterator

from . import jobs as _jobs
from ._jsonio import finite_loads

__all__ = ["publish", "get", "feasible"]

_VERSION = 1
_RESOURCE_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "region", "capacity", "start", "end",
                    "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
_RECORD_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version", "region", "capacity", "start",
                  "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "history", "idempotency", "audit")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "resource_id", "version")
_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"


class _Store:
    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}


def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = _Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _check_values(resource: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    region = resource["region"]
    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")

    capacity = resource["capacity"]
    if not _is_plain_int(capacity) or capacity <= 0:
        raise ValueError("capacity must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    for name in ("start", "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
        value = resource[name]
        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
                             "integer")
    if resource["start"] > resource["end"]:
        raise ValueError("start must not be later than end")

    residency = resource["residency"]
    if not isinstance(residency, list) or not residency:
        raise ValueError("residency must be a non-empty list")
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for entry in residency:
        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry:
            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
        if entry in seen:
            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
        seen.add(entry)
    # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
    if residency != sorted(residency):
        raise ValueError("residency regions must be sorted by code point")
    if region not in seen:
        raise ValueError("residency regions must contain the resource region")


def _normalize_resource(resource: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_RESOURCE_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("resource must be an object with exactly "
                         "resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, "
                         "unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency")

    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")

    normalized: dict[str, Any] = {
        "resource_id": resource_id,
        "region": resource["region"],
        "capacity": resource["capacity"],
        "start": resource["start"],
        "end": resource["end"],
        "unit_cost": resource["unit_cost"],
        "carbon_intensity": resource["carbon_intensity"],
        "residency": resource["residency"],
    }
    _check_values(normalized)
    normalized["residency"] = list(normalized["residency"])
    return normalized


def _check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
    keys = list(mapping)
    if keys != sorted(keys):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")


def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("supply file root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported supply file version")

    history_raw = data["history"]
    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
    audit_raw = data["audit"]
    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")

    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
                             "per resource")
        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
                raise ValueError("resource record has invalid fields")
            if record["resource_id"] != resource_id:
                raise ValueError("resource record id does not match its key")
            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
                    or record["version"] != index:
                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
            _check_values(record)
            if records and record["start"] <= records[-1]["start"]:
                raise ValueError("resource starts must increase across "
                                 "versions")
            records.append({
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": index,
                "region": record["region"],
                "capacity": record["capacity"],
                "start": record["start"],
                "end": record["end"],
                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(record["residency"]),
            })
        history[resource_id] = records

    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
                or resource_id not in history:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
                             "resource")
        idempotency[key] = resource_id

    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("publish audit event has invalid fields")
        event_key = event["key"]
        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
        event_version = event["version"]
        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
                or resource_id not in history:
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
                             "resource")
        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
                or event_version > len(history[resource_id]):
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
                             "version")
        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "resource_id": resource_id,
                       "version": event_version}

    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
    # idempotency key binds one resource and one publish event, the map
    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version
    # is bound to exactly one event.
    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
    for key, resource_id in idempotency.items():
        if events[key]["resource_id"] != resource_id:
            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
                             "entry")
    published = {(resource_id, record["version"])
                 for resource_id, records in history.items()
                 for record in records}
    bound = {(event["resource_id"], event["version"])
             for event in events.values()}
    if bound != published:
        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
                         "audit event")

    return history, idempotency, events


def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
]:
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return {}, {}, {}, None

    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
        data = finite_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    history, idempotency, events = _validate_structure(data)
    return history, idempotency, events, raw


def _serialize(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
    # surfaces chained after the original error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".resources-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
    # byte-for-byte.
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".resources-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise


def publish(
    path: str,
    resource: dict[str, object],
    idempotency_key: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.

    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.

    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.

    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
    version, structure, ordering or references) raises ``ValueError``;
    any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Calls serialize
    across threads and processes per resolved real path.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
                store.realpath)

            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
            if existing_id is not None:
                event = events[idempotency_key]
                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
                if {field: existing[field]
                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different resource")
                return dict(existing), False

            versions = history.get(resource_id)
            if versions is None:
                versions = []
                history[resource_id] = versions
                version = 1
            else:
                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
                                     "versions")
                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1

            record: dict[str, Any] = {
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
                "region": normalized["region"],
                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
                "start": normalized["start"],
                "end": normalized["end"],
                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
            }
            versions.append(record)
            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
            events[idempotency_key] = {
                "key": idempotency_key,
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
            }
            _commit_file(store.realpath,
                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
            return dict(record), True


def get(
    path: str,
    resource_id: str,
    version: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.

    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file raises ``ValueError``; an
    unknown resource id raises ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown
    version ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure
    raises ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record
    is a fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start,
    end, unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
    if version is not None \
            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
    if raw is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
    versions = history.get(resource_id)
    if versions is None:
        raise KeyError(resource_id)
    if version is None:
        return dict(versions[-1])
    if version > len(versions):
        raise KeyError(version)
    return dict(versions[version - 1])


def feasible(
    job_path: str,
    supply_path: str,
    job_id: str,
    at: int,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.

    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.

    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
    an invalid file raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``.

    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
    candidate the list is empty.
    """
    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))

        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
            job_real)
        if job_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
        if supply_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")

        job = accepted.get(job_id)
        if job is None:
            raise KeyError(job_id)

        work = job["work"]
        regions = set(job["regions"])
        residency = set(job["residency"])
        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for records in history.values():
            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
            for record in records:
                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
                    active = record
            if active is None:
                continue
            if active["region"] not in regions:
                continue
            if active["capacity"] < work:
                continue
            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
                continue
            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
                continue
            total_cost = work * active["unit_cost"]
            total_carbon = work * active["carbon_intensity"]
            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
                continue
            candidates.append({
                "resource": dict(active),
                "total_cost": total_cost,
                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
            })

    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (entry["resource"]["carbon_intensity"],
                                       entry["resource"]["unit_cost"],
                                       entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
    return candidates

1	"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process job registries.
2	
3	Two on-disk formats live side by side and are never converted into one
4	another:
5	
6	* :func:`register` serves the original field-sparse registry (version
7	  1) with job_id, deadline, energy_wh, residency_regions and state.
8	* :func:`submit` / :func:`get` serve complete scheduling-constraint
9	  jobs (version 2) with job_id, work, deadline, regions, residency,
10	  max_cost, carbon_cap and state, an idempotency map and, for every
11	  first acceptance, a submit audit event.
12	
13	A version-1 file handed to :func:`submit`/:func:`get` is an unsupported
14	version and raises ``ValueError`` with its bytes untouched, just as a
15	version-2 file handed to :func:`register` does; old ``jobs.register``
16	files are never upgraded.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import contextlib
22	import fcntl
23	import json
24	import os
25	import tempfile

76	def _normalize_job(job: object) -> tuple[str, int, int, list[str]]:
77	    if not isinstance(job, dict) or set(job.keys()) != _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
78	        raise ValueError("job must be an object with exactly job_id, deadline, "
79	                         "energy_wh and residency_regions")
80	
81	    job_id = job["job_id"]
82	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
83	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
84	
85	    deadline = job["deadline"]
86	    if not _is_plain_int(deadline) or deadline < 0:
87	        raise ValueError("deadline must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
88	
89	    energy_wh = job["energy_wh"]
90	    if not _is_plain_int(energy_wh) or energy_wh <= 0:
91	        raise ValueError("energy_wh must be a non-boolean positive integer")
92	
93	    regions = job["residency_regions"]
94	    if not isinstance(regions, list) or not regions:
95	        raise ValueError("residency_regions must be a non-empty list")
96	    normalized: list[str] = []
97	    seen: set[str] = set()
98	    for region in regions:
99	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
100	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
101	        if region in seen:
102	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
103	        seen.add(region)
104	        normalized.append(region)
105	    normalized.sort()  # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
106	
107	    return job_id, deadline, energy_wh, normalized

110	def _validate_regions(regions: object) -> list[str]:
111	    if not isinstance(regions, list) or not regions:
112	        raise ValueError("residency_regions must be a non-empty list")
113	    seen: set[str] = set()
114	    for region in regions:
115	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region or region in seen:
116	            raise ValueError("invalid residency region")
117	        seen.add(region)
118	    if regions != sorted(regions):
119	        raise ValueError("residency_regions are not normalized")
120	    return list(regions)

123	def _validate_structure(
124	    data: object,
125	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]:
126	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
127	        raise ValueError("registry root must be an object with keys "
128	                         "version, jobs and idempotency")
129	
130	    version = data["version"]
131	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
132	        raise ValueError("unsupported registry version")
133	
134	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
135	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
136	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict):
137	        raise ValueError("jobs and idempotency must be objects")
138	
139	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
140	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
141	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
142	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
143	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record.keys()) != set(_JOB_FIELDS):
144	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
145	        if record["job_id"] != name:
146	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
147	        if not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
148	            raise ValueError("job_id must be a string")
149	        if not _is_plain_int(record["deadline"]) or record["deadline"] < 0:
150	            raise ValueError("invalid deadline")
151	        if not _is_plain_int(record["energy_wh"]) or record["energy_wh"] <= 0:
152	            raise ValueError("invalid energy_wh")
153	        _validate_regions(record["residency_regions"])
154	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
155	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
156	        jobs[name] = dict(record)
157	
158	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
159	    referenced: set[str] = set()
160	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
161	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
162	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
163	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
164	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a registered job")
165	        if job_id in referenced:
166	            raise ValueError("job registered under more than one idempotency key")
167	        referenced.add(job_id)
168	        idempotency[key] = job_id
169	
170	    return jobs, idempotency

173	def _load(realpath: str) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]:
174	    try:
175	        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
176	            text = handle.read()
177	    except FileNotFoundError:
178	        return {}, {}
179	
180	    try:
181	        data = strict_loads(text)
182	    except ValueError as exc:
183	        raise ValueError(f"registry file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
184	    return _validate_structure(data)

187	def _atomic_write(
188	    realpath: str,
189	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
190	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
191	) -> None:
192	    payload = {
193	        "version": _VERSION,
194	        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
195	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
196	    }
197	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
198	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
199	
200	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
201	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-", suffix=".tmp")
202	    try:
203	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
204	            handle.write(text)
205	            handle.flush()
206	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
207	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
208	    except BaseException:
209	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
210	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
211	        raise
212	
213	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
214	    try:
215	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
216	    finally:
217	        os.close(dir_fd)

220	def register(
221	    path: str,
222	    job: dict[str, object],
223	    idempotency_key: str,
224	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
225	    """Register a job idempotently, persisting it as compact UTF-8 JSON.
226	
227	    Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries job_id, deadline,
228	    energy_wh, residency_regions (sorted by code point) and ``state`` set to
229	    ``"queued"``; ``created`` is ``True`` for a new registration and ``False``
230	    when the idempotency key replays an identical, normalized job.
231	    """
232	    if not isinstance(path, str):
233	        raise ValueError("path must be a string")
234	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
235	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
236	    job_id, deadline, energy_wh, regions = _normalize_job(job)
237	
238	    store = _get_store(path)
239	    with store.lock:
240	        jobs, idempotency = _load(store.realpath)
241	        record: dict[str, object] = {
242	            "job_id": job_id,
243	            "deadline": deadline,
244	            "energy_wh": energy_wh,
245	            "residency_regions": regions,
246	            "state": _STATE,
247	        }
248	
249	        existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
250	        if existing_id is not None:
251	            existing = jobs[existing_id]
252	            if existing != record:
253	                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
254	                                 "different job")
255	            return dict(existing), False
256	
257	        if job_id in jobs:
258	            raise ValueError("job_id is already registered under another "
259	                             "idempotency key")
260	
261	        jobs[job_id] = record
262	        idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
263	        _atomic_write(store.realpath, jobs, idempotency)
264	        return dict(record), True

272	@contextlib.contextmanager
273	def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
274	    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
275	    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
276	    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
277	    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
278	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
279	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
280	    try:
281	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
282	        try:
283	            yield
284	        finally:
285	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
286	    finally:
287	        os.close(fd)

357	def _validate_submit_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
358	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str], dict[str, dict[str, str]]
359	]:
360	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_ROOT_FIELDS):
361	        raise ValueError("acceptance file root must be an object with keys "
362	                         "version, jobs, idempotency and audit")
363	
364	    version = data["version"]
365	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _SUBMIT_VERSION:
366	        raise ValueError("unsupported acceptance file version")
367	
368	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
369	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
370	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
371	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) \
372	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
373	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
374	        raise ValueError("jobs, idempotency and audit must be objects")
375	    _check_sorted_keys(jobs_raw, "jobs")
376	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
377	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
378	
379	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
380	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
381	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
382	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
383	        if not isinstance(record, dict) \
384	                or set(record.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS):
385	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
386	        if record["job_id"] != name or not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
387	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
388	        if not _is_plain_int(record["work"]) or record["work"] <= 0:
389	            raise ValueError("invalid work")
390	        for field in ("deadline", "max_cost", "carbon_cap"):
391	            if not _is_plain_int(record[field]) or record[field] < 0:
392	                raise ValueError(f"invalid {field}")
393	        regions = _validate_region_field(record["regions"], "regions")
394	        residency = _validate_region_field(record["residency"], "residency")
395	        if not set(residency).issubset(regions):
396	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be a subset of regions")
397	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
398	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
399	        jobs[name] = {field: record[field] for field in _SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS}
400	
401	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
402	    referenced: set[str] = set()
403	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
404	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
405	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
406	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
407	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference an accepted "
408	                             "job")
409	        if job_id in referenced:
410	            raise ValueError("job accepted under more than one idempotency "
411	                             "key")
412	        referenced.add(job_id)
413	        idempotency[key] = job_id
414	
415	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
416	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
417	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
418	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
419	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
420	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_EVENT_FIELDS):
421	            raise ValueError("submit audit event has invalid fields")
422	        event_key = event["key"]
423	        job_id = event["job_id"]
424	        result = event["result"]
425	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
426	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
427	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
428	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference an accepted job")
429	        if result != _STATE:
430	            raise ValueError("audit event result must be queued")
431	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "job_id": job_id,
432	                       "result": result}
433	
434	    # The three sections describe one acceptance history: each
435	    # idempotency key binds one job and one submit event, every accepted
436	    # job has both, and the event and the map agree on the job.
437	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
438	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
439	    for key, job_id in idempotency.items():
440	        if events[key]["job_id"] != job_id:
441	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
442	                             "entry")
443	    if set(jobs) != referenced:
444	        raise ValueError("every accepted job must be bound to an "
445	                         "idempotency key")
446	
447	    return jobs, idempotency, events

450	def _load_submit_file(
451	    realpath: str,
452	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str],
453	           dict[str, dict[str, str]], bytes | None]:
454	    try:
455	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
456	            raw = handle.read()
457	    except FileNotFoundError:
458	        return {}, {}, {}, None
459	
460	    try:
461	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
462	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
463	        raise ValueError(
464	            f"acceptance file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
465	    try:
466	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
467	        data = finite_loads(text)
468	    except ValueError as exc:
469	        raise ValueError(
470	            f"acceptance file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
471	    jobs, idempotency, events = _validate_submit_structure(data)
472	    return jobs, idempotency, events, raw

477	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
478	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
479	) -> bytes:
480	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's

482	    payload = {
483	        "version": _SUBMIT_VERSION,
484	        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},

490	    return text.encode("utf-8")

493	def _rollback_submit_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
494	                          old_bytes: bytes | None,
495	                          first: BaseException) -> None:
496	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
497	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
498	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
499	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
500	    try:
501	        if old_bytes is None:
502	            try:
503	                os.unlink(realpath)
504	            except FileNotFoundError:
505	                pass
506	        else:
507	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
508	                dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
509	            try:
510	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
511	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
512	                    handle.flush()
513	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
514	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
515	            except BaseException:
516	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
517	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
518	                raise
519	        _fsync_directory(directory)
520	    except OSError as recovery:
521	        raise recovery from first
522

524	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
525	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
526	    try:
527	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
528	    finally:
529	        os.close(dir_fd)

532	def _commit_submit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
533	                        old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
534	    # One durable commit for jobs, the idempotency map and the audit
535	    # event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
536	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
537	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful submit leaves the original file
538	    # byte-for-byte.
539	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
540	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
541	        dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-submit-", suffix=".tmp")
542	    try:
543	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
544	            handle.write(payload)
545	            handle.flush()
546	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
547	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
548	    except BaseException as first:
549	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
550	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
551	        raise
552	    try:
553	        _fsync_directory(directory)
554	    except BaseException as first:
555	        _rollback_submit_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
556	        raise
